title: The second look: gallbladder wall, bile duct and bladder
summary: Four questions that come after you find the organ: is this thick gallbladder wall cholecystitis, is the bile duct dilated, is the bladder truly full and has it affected the kidneys, and is the material in the bladder clot or a lesion? Learn to measure correctly, use colour Doppler to separate duct from vessel, estimate bladder volume, and read each finding in context.
author: Dr Firas Abou-Auda, Consultant in Emergency Medicine and Course Director, Wavelength
conflicts: Dr Firas Abou-Auda is Course Director of Wavelength, which runs paid ultrasound courses.
audience: Emergency, acute and urgent care doctors, advanced clinical practitioners and physician associates who already find the gallbladder, kidneys and bladder, and want to answer the next question.
outcomes: Measure the gallbladder wall correctly and list the causes of wall thickening outside the gallbladder
Recognise the pattern of acute calculous cholecystitis
Identify the common bile duct with colour Doppler, measure it, and interpret it for age and cholecystectomy
Estimate bladder volume, check the kidneys and troubleshoot a catheter
Separate bladder clot from a wall lesion using movement and colour Doppler, and refer appropriately
